page text: Devin ran each of the 12 main-ladder problems once on swe-1-6-slow. It passed 6/12 (pass rate 50%), with a median 10.5 s per call. Timeouts: p04 taller_within, p11 best_average. Wrong answers: p06 calc, p07 weighted_distance_sums, p09 k_machine_schedule. Crashes: p12 sheet. It reports no tokens and no cost, so it has no $ per pass and appears on no $ chart, in no Winner pick and on no best-trade-offs line.
page text: Each family shows the lane with the closest pass rate. Ties use the closest median time, then cost per pass.

page text: Each full-run config ran 12 problems × 5 repeats (main + exploratory phases, repeats 1–5). 87 of the 201 Grok calls come from the first run. grok47-medium ran p01–p06 only, as before; it was not extended, so it is not in the closest-lane comparison. 1 call hit the time limit and counts as a miss: grok47-high on p12 repeat 5. A killed call has no bill, so that config's $ per pass is a floor. luna-high and sol61-high-fast did not run every problem in the main and exploratory phases, so they are left out of the comparison. CLI-reported cost; list price not used for Grok. Codex dollars use tokens × list price with the fast-mode multiplier. Closest lane = nearest pass rate among the full-ladder lanes, then nearest median time, then cost per pass.

page text: Not on these problems. Every Grok config is beaten on pass rate, speed and cost at once: grok47-high by 10 lanes (for example haiku-high, 60/60, 14.7 s, $0.0028 per pass). grok47-low by 11 lanes (for example haiku-high, 60/60, 14.7 s, $0.0028 per pass). grok47fast-low by 12 lanes (for example haiku-high, 60/60, 14.7 s, $0.0028 per pass). Grok passes more than luna-low, luna-low-bare, luna-medium, luna56-high and luna56-low. Every one of those lanes is faster and cheaper per pass. Grok costs less per pass than only astra-medium ⚡. Each of those passes more than the Grok config that undercuts it. Grok is faster than no lane.

page text: Don't use luna-low or luna-medium alone: they miss about 1 answer in 4.

page text: Four configs passed every try in every set. They were haiku-high, sonnet-medium, sol61-high and astra-medium. Repo tasks counted as task complete: hidden and visible tests both pass. haiku-high is the cheapest, at $0.0028 per pass.
page text: If speed matters most, use sonnet-medium. It takes 10.1 s to haiku-high's 14.7 s. sonnet-medium costs 4.4× as much per pass.

page text: On Codex's bench, both families gained. luna-low rose from 36 to 47 passes. It cost ~3× per pass and took ~3× the median time. haiku-low rose from 57 to 60 passes. It cost ~1.1× per pass, with the same median time.
page text: On L7, luna-high passed 15/15; sol56-high missed. luna-high cost ~$0.0015 per pass versus sol56-high's ~$0.069.
page text: On repo edits, sol61-high took 118 s; astra-medium took 66 s. sonnet-medium and haiku-low took about 28 s. Both Codex picks took over twice as long. All four completed every run.

page text: SemiAnalysis: Anthropic plans give ~5× OpenAI's API-priced value at the Opus/Sol tier. We price list-rate calls, not plan quotas, so we can’t test that. At list price, haiku-high beats sol61-high ~7× per pass; tiers differ. On repo tasks the gap is ~8×. luna-low costs least per run, but it completes 7/12 (12/12 hidden), so per complete task haiku-low is cheapest: $0.0051 against luna-low's $0.0056.

page text: Sol 6.1 high on fast was slower than Sol 5.6 high — does Terra high match or beat Sol 5.6 high on speed and pass rate? It is faster but misses. terra61-high takes 11.9 s to sol56-high's 14.5 s, and passes 58/60 to 60/60. The 2 misses are on p04 taller_within (repeats 1, 3). terra61-low matches sol56-high at 60/60 and is faster, 10.3 s. Cost per pass, list-price estimates: terra61-low ~$0.010, terra61-high ~$0.0079, sol56-high ~$0.042. Fast mode was not tried. The trigger was a low/high gap of 10 points or more, or terra high outside 0.5–2× of sol56-high's median. The gap is 3.3 points and the ratio is 0.82×, so it did not fire. Extra data, one repeat each: gpt-5.6-terra passed 12/12 at high and 9/12 at low.

page text: sol56-high is a generation older than sol61-high. Both pass every main-ladder try. sol56-high takes 14.5 s at ~$0.042 per pass. sol61-high takes 27.4 s at ~$0.019. ⚡ cuts that to 17.4 s, at ~$0.036. So the newer model is cheaper but slower. ⚡ does not close the gap.

Every task prompt told agents to add tests and that all tests must pass. All 6 failing tests in the 5 clean-home red runs are tests luna-low itself added, none a shipped test, and 0 runs edited the shipped tests. The audit reads 5 of the 6 red runs (clean-home and original) as wrong tests (the cache tests insert both entries at the same time, so both expire; the config tests expect behaviour the task does not ask for) and 1 as wrong code that the hidden suite missed (t1_discount accepts a boolean percentage; see the stricter-suite regrade below). The classification is still under audit until results/annotations.json carries the labels. Costs ranged from $0.0033 to $0.45 per run; per complete task luna-low costs $0.0056 against haiku-low's $0.0051.
